answer: A falcon-eyed registry can resist sybils by tying each agent identity to a refundable stake plus a slowly earned reputation: a new agent may join the river of transactions only with limited rate limits until it completes verifiable work, and its stake is slashed if peers attest fraud. Like an opal that gains value only when cut and polished over time, trust accrues gradually, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake agents must lock capital for every one and wait out the same slow ramp, making the attack costlier than any profit from gaming the market.
